facts.claim: Elevated levels of maternal cortisol late in gestation are linked to accelerated cognitive development and higher scores at 12 months.
facts.quote: Elevated levels of maternal cortisol late in gestation, however, were associated with accelerated cognitive development and higher scores at 12 months.

facts.claim: Exposure to high levels of cortisol early in pregnancy is linked to a slower rate of development over the 1st year and lower mental development scores at 12 months.
facts.quote: Exposure to elevated concentrations of cortisol early in gestation was associated with a slower rate of development over the 1st year and lower mental development scores at 12 months.

facts.claim: Chronic cortisol exposure can cause atrophy in stress-sensitive brain regions, such as the hippocampus and amygdala, affecting memory, fear responses, and executive function.
facts.quote: Structural changes in stress-sensitive brain regions, such as the hippocampus and amygdala, are common, as chronic cortisol exposure can cause atrophy in these areas, affecting memory, fear responses, and executive function.
facts.causalWarning: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

facts.claim: Low socioeconomic status in young children is linked to increased cortisol secretion.
facts.quote: Altogether, these results show that low SES in young children is related to increased cortisol secretion, although the impact of SES on cortisol secretion is absent after transition to high school.

facts.claim: Partial and total sleep deprivation makes plasma cortisol levels over the 1800-2300-hour period higher on day 2 than on day 1 (37 and 45% increases, p = 0. 03 and 0. 003, respectively).
facts.quote: After partial and total sleep deprivation, plasma cortisol levels over the 1800-2300-hour period were higher on day 2 than on day 1 (37 and 45% increases, p = 0. 03 and 0. 003, respectively)

research.angle: While chronic cortisol exposure can cause structural brain atrophy and prenatal cortisol levels can influence cognitive development, the effects of prenatal cortisol are inconsistent, with late-gestation exposure linked to accelerated development.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that cortisol levels are influenced by socioeconomic status, sleep loss, and prenatal conditions, and that chronic exposure can cause structural brain changes, but it does not specifically link standardized testing to these outcomes.
research.caveat: None of the provided sources specifically mention standardized testing or classroom environments.
